sources.title: UK Parliament, The Articles, constitution and trade
sources.note: Article 1 sets 1 May 1707 and name Great Britain; Article 3 one Parliament, Article 22 Scottish representation; short written English quotation.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Ratification of the Union 1706-07
sources.note: Scottish parliamentary ratification amid substantial protest; not unanimous consent.

sources.title: UK Parliament, United into One Kingdom
sources.note: Separate local Scottish structures continued; new taxes and Jacobite opposition challenged the 1707 union.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Original Act of Union with Ireland 1800
sources.note: Acts passed in 1800, effective 1 January 1801; Irish Parliament ended; formal name included Great Britain and Ireland.

sources.title: House of Commons Library, The United Kingdom and independence
sources.note: Careful timeline of 1707, 1801, Irish Free State 1922 and Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act 1927.

sources.title: British Museum, Sir Hans Sloane
sources.note: Early eighteenth-century physician promoted smallpox inoculation; his collection helped found British Museum and was entangled with Jamaican plantation slavery.

sources.title: Historic England, Education Buildings
sources.note: Ackworth Quaker boarding school 1778 and Georgian school arrangements, including monitors and small schoolrooms; examples not universal schooling.

sources.title: Historic England, Georgian and Victorian Terraced Housing
sources.note: Georgian urban townhouses could separate basement kitchens and service spaces from reception rooms; class-specific built environment.

sources.title: Historic England, Coalhouse Point Archaeological Survey
sources.note: Appendix records a Georgian Staffordshire chamber pot found at East Tilbury, c.1765-95; a local object, not a national toilet census.

sources.title: Science Museum, James Watt, office equipment and high-street fashion
sources.note: Watt and Boulton steam engines used for industrial power in late eighteenth-century Birmingham; later factory growth; Watt improved engines, did not invent steam.

sources.title: Science and Industry Museum, Langworthy Brothers
sources.note: Manchester cotton manufacturing growth from around 1780; mechanization and dependence on cotton grown by enslaved people overseas.

sources.title: Historic England, Black Lives in England: Servants
sources.note: Pero, an enslaved servant brought from Nevis to eighteenth-century Bristol; one life that challenges an all-white or slavery-free Georgian story.

sources.title: UK Parliament, The Transatlantic Slave Trade
sources.note: British participation in slave trade; 1807 trading ban, 1833 abolition statute effective 1834; owners compensated, formerly enslaved people not.

sources.title: Science and Industry Museum, 1830: A rebellious year
sources.note: 1830 Liverpool and Manchester Railway alongside industrial cotton growth, mill hardship and demands for representation.

sources.title: Science and Industry Museum, Ancoats: From cotton to cool
sources.note: Manchester Ancoats workers housing, archaeological domino, 1831 cholera and more than half of houses lacking plumbing; local case.

sources.title: UK Parliament, The Great Famine
sources.note: Irish Great Famine 1845-52, potato blight, starvation, illness, mass emigration and British government response; avoid reducing causes to crop disease alone.

sources.title: Historic England, Public Conveniences at Guilford Place
sources.note: 1851 Great Exhibition charged one penny to use toilets; 1855 London municipal facilities; Victorian women had much poorer public access.

sources.title: UK Parliament, The 1870 Education Act
sources.note: School boards in England and Wales 1870, similar Scottish law 1872, compulsory attendance five to ten in 1880, fees to 1891; poor children often worked.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Parliament and Empire 1815-1970
sources.note: British empire and independence chronology, including Indian independence 1947 and multiple African and Caribbean states 1957-70; colonies had their own peoples and agency.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Home Front in the First World War
sources.note: Defence of the Realm Act, blackouts, air raids and food rationing affected British civilian life during WWI.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Suffrage in wartime
sources.note: Women took new war jobs 1914-18; this did not by itself cause suffrage and exclusions persisted.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Women get the vote
sources.note: 1918 some women over 30 with property qualification got vote; 1928 equal voting age 21; men gained wider franchise in 1918.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Towards Home Rule
sources.note: Irish demands for home rule, war, 1921 treaty, 1922 Free State and Northern Ireland partition.

sources.title: House of Lords Library, Government of Ireland Act 1920
sources.note: Partition and Northern Ireland opt-out from Irish Free State on 7 December 1922.

sources.title: UK Parliament, Royal and Parliamentary Titles Bill 1927
sources.note: 1927 parliamentary debate on change to Great Britain and Northern Ireland formal title after Irish Free State.

sources.title: Imperial War Museums, VE Day Learning Resource
sources.note: British WWII civilian food and clothing shortages; food rationing began January 1940, children had extra clothing coupons by 1942.

sources.title: Imperial War Museums, Evacuation of Children in Britain 1939-1944
sources.note: IWM record documents wartime evacuation of children from danger areas; experiences differed.

sources.title: NHS England, Milestones of the NHS
sources.note: NHS founded 1948 with care free at point of delivery; West Indies staff recruitment 1949; later vaccinations and CT scanning milestones.

sources.title: The National Archives, Postwar Caribbean Migration
sources.note: 1948 Windrush passenger list and nationality law; Caribbean migrants helped rebuild Britain while facing job and housing discrimination; Windrush not first ship.

sources.title: The National Archives, Commonwealth Migration since 1945
sources.note: Some migrants travelled ahead of family, faced housing shortage and racism; Caribbean arrivals predated Windrush.

sources.title: House of Commons Library, Introduction to Devolution in the UK
sources.note: 1998 statutory frameworks and distinct Scottish, Welsh, Northern Irish devolved powers; Westminster retains reserved matters.

sources.title: House of Commons Library, Belfast/Good Friday Agreement at 25
sources.note: 1998 agreement after Troubles, power sharing, identity rights and consent principle; not claim conflict instantly vanished.

sources.title: Welsh Government, Welsh Language (Wales) Measure 2011
sources.note: 2011 measure gave Welsh official status in Wales and public-service duties; many UK languages exist.

sources.title: Welsh Government, Welsh-language explanation of equality legislation
sources.note: Welsh text includes short phrase rhoi statws swyddogol i’r Gymraeg yng Nghymru (give Welsh official status in Wales); original-language sample.

sources.title: St George’s NHS Trust, 40 years of CT scanning
sources.note: World first patient CT scan at Atkinson Morley Hospital, Wimbledon, October 1971; medical innovation in a specific hospital.

proposedOverrides.summary: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland began in 1801. Industrial power and imperial reach grew, while slavery, famine, inequality and demands for Irish self-government shaped its people’s lives. Most of Ireland became the Irish Free State in 1922; the formal royal and parliamentary title changed in 1927. The state and its people continued under a different territorial name.

proposedOverrides.summary: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland is a continuing state. Its twentieth- and twenty-first-century history includes world war, the NHS, migration, the end of most colonial rule, devolved government and many living languages. The map’s 1938 start is a snapshot date, not the country’s founding.
